author: Sample commentary (synthetic data)
headline: Where a program cost can be tied to a measure, unit costs rose faster than inflation in most service areas.
paragraphs: Cost per outcome divides a program's actual spending by the number of units its measure counts (placements, visits, repairs). It works only for count measures with a clearly linked program budget; percentages and rates are excluded, and the mapping is listed in the data notes.

Rising unit cost can mean lower productivity, harder cases, or a deliberate shift to more intensive services; the view shows the trend and leaves the interpretation to the reader, with the department's own explanation where one exists.

templates.template: {measures_fmt} measures with a linked cost, {depts_fmt} departments: median change in real cost per unit FY{fy0}–FY{fy1} is {median_change}.
templates.fallback: Too few records match to summarize; widen the years or clear a filter.

caveats.text: Program-to-measure links are the analyst's judgment; a different mapping gives different unit costs. Each link's rationale is in DATA_NOTES.
